classification.self_injury: Post-hoc: <=14 regular-season offensive game appearances, verified primarily from play-participation data, plus at least one later Out/Doubtful injury report.
classification.teammate_injury_opportunity: Post-hoc: non-first-team player whose higher-ranked opening teammate had >=2 Out/Doubtful weeks and whose own weekly opportunity rose by >=25% and >=2 opportunity units during those weeks.
classification.stable_no_shock: Neither conservative self-injury nor teammate-injury-opportunity flag.

interpretation.primary: Subsequent injuries do not explain away FFToday's remaining overall advantage. Native V2 performs exceptionally well in the post-hoc self-injury cohort, so including those seasons improves Native's headline relative standing. Removing conservatively identified injury-affected player-seasons makes FFToday's relative advantage larger.
interpretation.teammate_opportunity: Injury-created opportunity for backups is a real Native weakness in this sample: FFToday wins 21 of 32 eligible groups among 27 conservatively flagged player-seasons.
interpretation.causality_caution: The self-injury result does not prove Native predicts injuries. It may reflect legitimate durability information, more conservative volume forecasts, regression/shrinkage, or favorable alignment with realized missed time. Conditioning on future injury status is itself a selection operation, so the full-season benchmark remains the primary real-world accuracy score.

next_model_implication: Do not adjust or remove injury seasons from the primary benchmark. Investigate injury-created opportunity/backup workload forecasting as a targeted future feature problem, and separately test whether Native's self-injury advantage comes from calibrated preseason durability risk or generic conservative projection bias.
